quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #6
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: Is it safe to stop on railroad tracks for a short time while moving with other vehicles?

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: Never stop, stand, or park on railroad tracks. Only cross railroad tracks if your entire vehicle can fit on the other side.

questions.question: How should you avoid hitting vehicles in your blind spots?

options.text: Turn your head and look over your shoulder before changing lanes.
Adjust your rearview mirrors every few minutes.
Honk your horn before turning or changing lanes.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Before turning or changing lanes, turn your head and glance over your shoulder to see if your blind spot is clear. Do not rely only on mirrors.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop sign ahead.
Railroad crossing ahead.
Construction ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing ahead.
questions.explanation: A round sign always means a railroad crossing is coming.

questions.question: What often happens when you brake hard continuously on ice and snow?

options.text: You stop faster.
Your front wheels lock up and you lose steering control.
Your brakes stay from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your front wheels lock up and you lose steering control.
questions.explanation: Hard braking on snow and ice can lock your front wheels, causing you to lose steering. Slow down ahead of time to avoid hard braking.

questions.question: What does a double solid yellow line down the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions. Drivers cannot pass.
Traffic moves in opposite directions. Drivers can pass when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Drivers cannot pass.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Drivers can pass when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in opposite directions. Drivers cannot pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Solid yellow lines mean no passing is allowed.

questions.question: At a stop sign, what should you do after stopping?

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for cars behind you.
Move when the car ahead moves.
Look right, then left, then right again.
Look left, then right, then left again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look left, then right, then left again.
questions.explanation: Look left first because vehicles from the left are closer to you. Then look right. Finally, look left again to check for any vehicles you might have missed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop sign ahead.
Side road.
Railroad warning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop sign ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a stop sign is coming up.

questions.question: What type of sign is diamond-shaped?

options.text: Road hazard sign.
Interstate route sign.
School crossing sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road hazard sign.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually diamond-shaped and yellow (orange in work areas). They warn you about hazards or special rules ahead.

questions.question: How do you know where traffic is behind you?

options.text: Check your rearview mirror often.
Turn and look out your back window.
Keep other vehicles out of your blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your rearview mirror often.
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirror regularly to know where traffic behind you is located.

questions.question: If your turn signals stop working, what should you use to show you are turning?

options.text: Your horn
Your headlights
Hand signals
Your emergency flashers

questions.correctAnswerText: Hand signals
questions.explanation: Use hand signals to show when you plan to turn if your turn signals do not work.

questions.question: You notice a vehicle defect that may affect safe operation. What should you do?

options.text: Fix the defect as soon as possible.
Fix the defect when you have money.
Drive slowly.
Drive normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fix the defect as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Fix any defect that may affect safe operation right away. Fix it before you drive the vehicle.

questions.question: When can you pass by driving on the right shoulder of the road?

options.text: When there are no pedestrians nearby.
When the car in front is driving too slowly.
When the car in front is turning.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Do not drive off the pavement or onto the shoulder to pass another vehicle. Never pass on the right shoulder.

questions.question: Your wheels slip off the edge of the road. What should you do?

options.text: Jerk the steering wheel to force your vehicle back onto the road.
Speed up and steer back onto the road slowly.
Slam on the brakes and stop.
Gently brake and slowly turn the steering wheel to get back on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently brake and slowly turn the steering wheel to get back on the road.
questions.explanation: Reduce speed by gently applying the brakes. Then slowly turn the steering wheel to return to the road at a safe speed. Do not jerk the steering wheel.

questions.question: What do work zone signs mean?

options.text: It is summer.
You must stop and back up immediately.
Driving conditions are not ideal.
Drive faster to leave the work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving conditions are not ideal.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs are orange. They show that work is happening on or near the road. Be very careful when you see these signs.

questions.question: What happens when drivers eat or drink while driving?

options.text: They make no mistakes.
They have trouble driving slowly.
They drive better because they are not hungry.
They have trouble controlling their vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They have trouble controlling their vehicles.
questions.explanation: Eating, drinking, or smoking while driving is dangerous. These actions take your hands off the wheel and eyes off the road. Drivers who do these things have trouble staying in their lanes and controlling their vehicles.

questions.question: As you drive faster, what is important to do?

options.text: Turn on your headlights.
Look far ahead of your vehicle.
Change lanes often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look far ahead of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds mean longer stopping distances. At high speeds, look far ahead so you have time to react to hazards safely.

questions.question: What problems do worn or bald tires cause?

options.text: Turning becomes harder.
They are more likely to hydroplane.
They increase stopping distance.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Worn or bald tires increase stopping distance and make turning harder. They also increase the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines in the middle of the road mean?

options.text: Railroad crossing ahead.
Pedestrian crossing ahead.
No one can pass from either direction.
Anyone can pass from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: No one can pass from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean you cannot pass from either direction. You may only cross these lines to turn left or pass pedestrians, bicyclists, scooter riders, or skateboarders when it is safe.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on an interstate?

options.text: Stop on the shoulder if you are tired.
Always use cruise control.
Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.
Change lanes often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Always signal, check your mirrors, and check your blind spot before changing lanes. Only stop on the shoulder for emergencies. Avoid changing lanes often. Do not use cruise control in heavy traffic or bad weather.

questions.question: When can you go through a stop sign with no stop line or crosswalk?

options.text: After slowing down to check for cross traffic.
After coming to a complete stop and checking that it is safe.
After stopping at least 20 feet before the intersection.
After slowing down to 10 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: After coming to a complete stop and checking that it is safe.
questions.explanation: Stop completely at any stop sign. If there is no stop line or crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection. Only proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: What is the speed limit in a residential area if no other speed limit is posted?

options.text: 45 mph
35 mph
25 mph
15 mph

questions.correctAnswerText: 25 mph
questions.explanation: In residential areas, the speed limit is 25 mph. If a different speed is posted, follow that posted speed instead.

questions.question: Who must wear a seat belt in a moving vehicle?

options.text: Only the driver
Only adult passengers
Only child passengers
Everyone in the vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: Everyone in the vehicle
questions.explanation: Everyone in a moving vehicle must wear a seat belt. Some children may need special safety seats instead.

questions.question: When is it illegal to drive below the speed limit?

options.text: When slow driving blocks the normal flow of traffic
When in heavy traffic in a construction zone
Only when driving in rural areas
When driving in bad weather

questions.correctAnswerText: When slow driving blocks the normal flow of traffic
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive so slowly that you block normal traffic. You can get a ticket for driving too slowly.

questions.question: When backing up, what should you do?

options.text: Rely only on your mirrors
Flash your lights
Open your door to see if it is safe
Turn your head and look out the rear window

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look out the rear window
questions.explanation: Always check behind your vehicle before backing. Turn your head to look through the rear window. Mirrors alone are not enough. Children and small objects are hard to see from the driver's seat.

questions.question: What should you do if your accelerator gets stuck while driving?

options.text: Reach down and try to pull it up
Shift to park
Shift to neutral and press the brake firmly
Turn off the engine

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to neutral and press the brake firmly
questions.explanation: If the accelerator sticks, keep your eyes on the road. Shift into neutral and press the brake pedal steadily. Then pull off the road when safe and turn off the engine.

questions.question: What affects how much space you need to cross traffic?

options.text: Road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic
The presence of a stop sign
Using your turn signals
Cars behind you

questions.correctAnswerText: Road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic
questions.explanation: The space you need to cross traffic depends on the road conditions, weather, and how much oncoming traffic there is.

questions.question: What should you do if traffic lights are out due to a power outage?

options.text: Park your car off the road and wait for power to return
Use hand signals to show other drivers what you will do
Turn on hazard lights and go through without stopping
Treat it like a four-way stop

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a four-way stop
questions.explanation: When a traffic light is out, treat the intersection as a four-way stop. Yield to other drivers, and go through when it is your turn.

questions.question: If bad weather makes it hard to see, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to get off the road quickly
Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic
Stay farther behind other vehicles

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther behind other vehicles
questions.explanation: In bad weather or darkness, increase your distance from other vehicles. This gives you more time to react to hazards you cannot see yet.

questions.question: You are in a left turn lane at an intersection with oncoming traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Move to the left of the center lane
Signal before you reach the intersection
Turn your front wheels left to get ready

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal before you reach the intersection
questions.explanation: Signal about 100 feet before turning. Keep your front wheels straight until it is safe to turn. This prevents another car from pushing you into oncoming traffic if it hits you from behind.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing red light?

options.text: Slow down and yield the right-of-way
Slow down and drive carefully through
Stop completely, check traffic, then go when safe

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, check traffic, then go when safe
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. Stop completely, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, then go when it is safe.
